title: Expressing sin(3*pi/2 - x) in Terms of sin x and cos x
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Express the quantity \sin(3\pi/2 - x) in terms of \sin x and \cos x.

steps.title: Apply the Sine Difference Formula
steps.explanation: Use sin(A - B) = sin A cos B - cos A sin B with A = 3*pi/2 and B = x.
steps.why: The sine difference identity separates the constant angle 3*pi/2 from the variable x.

steps.title: Evaluate Sine and Cosine at 3*pi/2
steps.explanation: At 3*pi/2 radians, the terminal point on the unit circle is (0, -1).
steps.why: Three-quarters of a counterclockwise revolution reaches the negative y-axis.

steps.title: Substitute and Simplify
steps.explanation: Substitute -1 and 0 into the expansion to obtain -cos x.
steps.why: The second term vanishes and the first simplifies to -cos x.
